title: traffic-throttle-and-roll-forward-matrix-for-experiments
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Define a prescriptive traffic throttling schedule and roll-forward decision matrix for A/B tests, canaries, and incremental feature rollouts that balances rapid iteration with customer safety. This ticket captures milestone definitions, metric gating rules, the automation hooks for rollback/roll-forward, and required dashboards and alerts. The output will be a deployable YAML matrix used by the rollout controller plus a short playbook for on-call/PM/Eng action in each gate state.
background: Current ad-hoc canaries vary across teams, causing inconsistent time-to-detection and uneven customer exposure. We need a standardized template that product teams can reuse for model/API changes and feature flags. The matrix should be compatible with console routing policies (region, tier), include quality and infra gates, and support both time-window and event-driven decisions.
milestones: Milestone 1: Define signal taxonomy and owners (quality, infra, business).
Milestone 2: Draft traffic throttling schedule (percent increments + duration windows).
Milestone 3: Implement automation hooks for the rollout controller and feature-flag service.
Milestone 4: Instrument dashboards and set gating alerts in Console (cost, latency, quality).
Milestone 5: Run shadow sweep + smoke canary on staging and iterate matrix thresholds.
Milestone 6: Publish template and run first pilot with search-relevance model swap.
traffic_schedule: Baseline collection window: 72h pre-rollout. Canary steps: 0% -> 1% for 2h (min 1000 requests), evaluate; 1% -> 5% for 6h, evaluate; 5% -> 20% for 12h, evaluate; 20% -> 50% for 24h, evaluate; 50% -> 100% for 24-48h. Each step requires a green signal on both quality and infra gates. Automated rollback if a critical gate trips.
signal_definitions: Infra gate: p95 latency increase > 40% relative to baseline OR error rate (5xx + model timeouts) > 0.7% absolute -> RED

Quality gate: automated evaluation set quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy/semantic_score depending on workload) worse by > 3% absolute OR hallucination-rate worse by > 2pp -> YELLOW/RED depending on magnitude
Business gate: conversion/engagement drop > 5% over window (for user-facing features) -> YELLOW
Cost gate: token cost per request > baseline + 35% -> YELLOW
Grace window: transient spikes under 15 minutes marked as transient unless sustained for > 3 consecutive evaluation windows.
decision_matrix: Green: progress to next step automatically after evaluation window. Yellow: hold at current step and notify owners; require explicit PM/Eng approval to progress. Red: auto-roll back to last safe step and page on-call SRE + PM. For combined signals, the worst-state wins (RED > YELLOW > GREEN). Escalation timeline: immediate page on RED, 30min follow-up on persistent YELLOW.
automation_hooks: Rollout controller endpoint for applying percent changes (integration with feature-flag service).
Webhook to create a rollback runbook entry in incident tracker when RED occurs.
Automated snapshot of model inputs and outputs for 1% sample when QUALITY gate trips for triage and offline evals.
Auto-annotated traces pushed to tracing service with tag rollout_id for 100% of failed requests during canary steps.
dashboards_and_alerts: Canary summary dashboard: per-step latency, error, cost, and quality delta compared to baseline (p50/p95/p99).
Signal heatmap view for combined gates across cohorts and regions.
Alert rules: RED->P1 page; YELLOW->Slack channel + email to owners; repeated YELLOW (3 windows) escalates to RED.
acceptance_criteria: Template YAML validated in staging and used by at least one pilot rollout.
Console dashboard shows canary summary with automatic compare-to-baseline for the last 72h.
Automation correctly executes a rollback on induced RED in staging and records snapshot artifacts for triage.
Runbook exists describing manual override steps, owner contacts, and postmortem checklist.
